input: This executive summary looks at a possible heat-recovery retrofit at a food plant and at whether the project should move forward at this stage. The plant currently uses 2074 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, which is a substantial part of the overall picture being considered here. According to the equipment vendor, the retrofit is projected to save 12% of that electricity use, which works out to a derived saving of 249 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $409k. Using an electricity price of $0.12 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $30k, and the derived simple payback therefore comes out at 13.6 years, and a 13.6-year payback is a long period over which to recover the investment. It is very important to emphasise that the saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, so it carries a significant degree of uncertainty. In addition, the refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, which means that the period of highest demand is not properly represented in the figures as they currently stand. Against this background, the recommendation of this summary is that a metered trial should be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, and the plant engineer will own the trial and will be responsible for reporting its results.
target: The recommendation is a metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision; the plant engineer owns the trial. The plant uses 2074 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. The vendor projects that a heat-recovery retrofit would save 12% of that use, a derived saving of 249 MWh per year at the vendor figure, at a capital cost of $409k. At an electricity price of $0.12 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $30k and the derived simple payback is 13.6 years. The payback rests on an unmeasured figure. The saving is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and the refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the highest-load period is absent from the evidence behind the projection. A payback of 13.6 years computed from a projection of that standing does not support a capital decision in either direction. The trial replaces the projection with a measurement on one line, at the cost of metering rather than of the retrofit, and its result scales to the full refrigeration load with the peak-month gap stated. The capital decision should wait for the trial figure. The trial also fixes the second weakness in the case. Metering one line through the peak month measures the load shape that the projection omitted, so the scaled saving that follows the trial rests on the plant's own refrigeration behaviour across the full load range, rather than on an annual average applied to a peak that was never examined.
